title: continuous-batcher-scheduler-tuning-queueing-fairness-starvation-timeouts
author: Jordan Li
body: Motivation: Production traffic patterns revealed occasional starvation and elevated tail latency in the continuous batcher under mixed short/long request workloads. SLOs were being impacted by head-of-line blocking when large sequences entered the queue and by aggressive per-request timeouts that caused wasted GPU capacity. This PR tunes the continuous-batcher scheduler to improve queueing fairness, reduce starvation of small/low-latency requests, and make timeouts more robust. Summary of changes: 1) Introduces a multi-queue scheduler: separate hot/small-request queue (latency-sensitive) and bulk/large-request queue with controlled draining. 2) Implements weighted fair dequeueing with starvation prevention counters and adaptive promotion of aged items. 3) Adds per-queue dynamic timeouts: requests get a base timeout based on request-size quantiles plus jitter; long-running requests are optionally extended when they are actively being serviced to avoid mid-response aborts. 4) Exposes two new runtime config knobs (continuous_batcher.queue_ratio and continuous_batcher.starvation_threshold_ms) behind a feature flag to stage rollout. 5) Instrumentation: adds metrics for queue lengths per-class, average wait time, starvation_events_total, timeout_abort_total and tracing spans for scheduler decisions. 6) Tests: unit tests for queue ordering, integration test that replays production traffic trace and checks P50/P99, and stress test for mixed workloads. Implementation notes: - The scheduler now maintains two lock-free ring buffers to avoid contention hotspots seen in the single-queue implementation. - Dequeue fairness is implemented using a configurable token-bucket-style allocator that gives the latency-sensitive queue priority tokens up to a configured ratio; tokens can be borrowed by the bulk queue when idle. - Starvation prevention uses an age-based promotion path: once a request crosses starvation_threshold_ms it is bumped to the front of the next dequeue cycle and the event is logged. - Timeout logic decouples "enqueue timeout" (how long we allow waiting in queue) from "service timeout" (how long the model is allowed to produce output) to avoid aborting in-progress generation. Performance results: On a mixed production-like trace (70% short < 64 tokens, 30% long > 1024 tokens) running on p4d instances: - End-to-end P50 improved from 12ms -> 8ms (33% reduction) - End-to-end P99 improved from 420ms -> 260ms (38% reduction) - Observed starvation_events_total dropped by ~92% after tuning thresholds - Overall GPU utilization remained within 3% of baseline; token throughput unchanged. Rollout plan: Feature-flagged rollout to 10% of serving fleet for 48h with enhanced metrics; if stable, increase to 50% then full rollout. Backward compatibility: Config defaults mirror current behavior; if the feature flag is off, behavior is identical to the existing single-queue scheduler. Security & safety: No change to request payload or LLM outputs. No user-facing API changes. Testing: Unit tests added and validated in CI, integration replay tests run against perf-canary cluster, DB migration: none. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked: ENG-2345 - [x] Unit/integration tests - [x] Metrics and traces added - [x] Feature-flagged rollout - [x] Performance numbers collected Additional notes: This PR also includes minor docs updates in the observability-pack to surface new metrics; follow-up PR will add console dashboards for queue-class metrics.

release_notes: Continuous batcher scheduler tuned: multi-queue scheduling with weighted fairness, starvation prevention, decoupled timeouts, new observability metrics. Improves P50/P99 latency for mixed workloads and reduces starvation events. Feature-flagged rollout.
